about: Cases for classifyFetchFailure: what a failed fetch's stderr means. The stderr strings are real git output, trimmed. Every implementation of the protocol maps each case to `expected`.

cases.name: ref missing at the authority
cases.stderr: fatal: couldn't find remote ref refs/locks/x

cases.name: refspec matched nothing
cases.stderr: error: src refspec refs/locks/x did not match any refs

cases.name: local ref lock held by another process
cases.stderr: error: cannot lock ref 'refs/locks/x': Unable to create '/tmp/reader/.git/refs/locks/x.lock': File exists.

cases.name: local directory/file ref clash (permanent, not retried)
cases.stderr: error: cannot lock ref 'refs/locks/x': 'refs/locks' exists; cannot create 'refs/locks/x'

cases.name: local ref moved under the fetch (not retried)
cases.stderr: error: cannot lock ref 'refs/locks/x': is at 9f8e7d6 but expected 1a2b3c4

cases.name: authority unreachable
cases.stderr:
fatal: '/tmp/nowhere' does not appear to be a git repository
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
